abilities.name: Divine Magic
abilities.prose:
See Spells for full details on divine magic.
Holy symbol: A cleric must carry a holy symbol (see Adventuring Gear).
Deity disfavour: Clerics must be faithful to the tenets of their alignment, clergy, and religion. Clerics who fall from favour with their deity may incur penalties.
Magical research: A cleric of any level may spend time and money on magical research. This allows them to create new spells or other magical effects associated with their deity. When a cleric reaches 9th level, they are also able to create magic items.
Spell casting: Once a cleric has proven their faith (from 2nd level), the character may pray to receive spells. The level progression table (below) shows the number of spells a cleric may memorize, based on their experience level. The list of spells available to clerics is found in Cleric Spells.
Using magic items: As spell casters, clerics can use magic scrolls of spells on their spell list. They can also use items that may only be used by divine spell casters (e.g. some magic staves).

abilities.name: Turning the Undead
abilities.prose: Clerics can invoke the power of their deity to repel undead monsters encountered. To turn the undead, the player rolls 2d6. The referee then consults the table below, comparing the roll against the HD of the type of undead monsters targeted.

abilities.name: Back-stab
abilities.prose: When attacking an unaware opponent from behind, a thief receives a +4 bonus to hit and doubles any damage dealt.

abilities.name: Read Languages
abilities.prose: A thief of 4th level or higher can read non-magical text in any language (including dead languages and basic codes) with 80% probability. If the roll fails, the thief may not try to read the same text again before gaining an experience level.

abilities.name: Scroll Use
abilities.prose: A thief of 10th level or higher can cast arcane spells from scrolls. There is a 10% chance of error: an unusual or deleterious effect instead of the expected effect.

spells.name: Cure Light Wounds
spells.range: The caster or a creature touched

spells.name: Cure Serious Wounds
spells.range: The caster or a creature touched

spells.name: Dispel Evil
spells.duration: Concentration (up to 1 turn) or instant (see below)

spells.name: Fly
spells.range: The caster or a creature touched

spells.name: Infravision
spells.range: The caster or a creature touched

spells.name: Invisibility
spells.duration: Permanent (but may be broken, see below)

spells.name: Invisibility 10’ Radius
spells.duration: Permanent (but may be broken, see below)

spells.name: Neutralize Poison
spells.range: The caster or a creature or object touched

spells.name: Quest
spells.duration: Until quest is completed / Instant (remove quest)

spells.name: Remove Curse
spells.range: The caster or a creature touched

spells.name: Remove Curse
spells.range: The caster or a creature touched

spells.name: Remove Fear
spells.range: The caster or a creature touched

sleep.name: Sleep

modes.prose: A single creature with 4+1 Hit Dice (see Hit point modifiers).
A total of 2d8 Hit Dice of creatures of 4 HD or lower each.

sleep.intro: Causes creatures (except undead) to fall into a magical slumber. The spell may target either:

cure_light_wounds.name: Cure Light Wounds
cure_light_wounds.range: The caster or a creature touched

reversed_form.name: Cause Light Wounds
reversed_form.prose: Inflicts 1d6+1 hit points of damage to a touched creature. In combat, a melee attack roll is required.

modes.prose: Inflicts 1d6+1 hit points of damage to a touched creature. In combat, a melee attack roll is required.
Healing a living subject: Restores 1d6+1 hit points of damage. This cannot raise the subject’s hit points above their normal maximum.
Curing paralysis: Paralysing effects are negated.

goblin.name: Goblin
goblin.intro: Small, grotesque humanoids with pallid, earth-coloured skin and glowing, red eyes. Dwell underground.

abilities.name: Hate the sun
abilities.prose: -1 to-hit in full daylight.

abilities.name: Wolf riders
abilities.prose: 20% of goblin groups encountered have wolf riders: ¼ of the group mounted on dire wolves.

abilities.name: Hate [dwarves](/srd/index.php/Dwarf_(Monster) "Dwarf (Monster)")
abilities.prose: Attack on sight.

abilities.name: Goblin king and bodyguards
abilities.prose: A 3HD (15hp) king and 2d6 2HD (2d6hp) bodyguards live in the goblin lair. They do not suffer attack penalties in daylight. The king gains a +1 bonus to damage.

abilities.name: Hoard
abilities.prose: Only have treasure type C when encountered in the wilderness or in their lair.

green_slime.name: Green Slime
green_slime.intro: Dripping, green slime that clings to walls and ceilings.

abilities.name: Surprise
abilities.prose: Drops down on surprised characters from above.

abilities.name: Acid
abilities.prose: When in contact with a victim, sticks on and exudes acid. The acid destroys wood or metal (including armour) in 6 rounds, but cannot affect stone.

abilities.name: Consume flesh
abilities.prose: Once in contact with flesh for 6 rounds, the victim is turned into green slime in a further 1d4 rounds.

abilities.name: Removing
abilities.prose: Once stuck on a victim, can only be removed by fire. This inflicts half damage to the victim and half to the slime.

abilities.name: Immunity
abilities.prose: Unharmed by all attacks except cold or fire.

abilities.name: Breath weapon
abilities.prose: 60’ long line of acid.

abilities.name: [Language](/srd/index.php/Languages "Languages") and spells
abilities.prose: 20%; 4 × 1st level.

abilities.name: Behaviour
abilities.prose: Chaotic dragons usually try to eat humans, but may sometimes capture them. Neutral dragons may attack or ignore humans. Lawful dragons may aid parties worthy of the honour.

abilities.name: Pride
abilities.prose: Dragons are immensely proud creatures and will always listen to flattery.

abilities.name: Attack pattern
abilities.prose: A dragon always attacks first with its breath weapon, then either breathes again or makes melee attacks (equal chance of either).

abilities.name: Energy immunity
abilities.prose: Unharmed by their own breath weapon or lesser versions thereof. Automatically save versus similar attack forms. (For example, a red dragon is immune to flaming oil and suffers half damage from fire ball spells.)

abilities.name: Subduing
abilities.prose: Will surrender if reduced to 0hp by non-lethal attacks (see Subduing), admitting that it has been defeated. (Subdual damage does not reduce the damage done by the breath weapon.) A subdued dragon will attempt to escape or attack its captors, if the opportunity presents itself or if given a suicidal command. A subdued dragon may be sold for up to 1,000gp per hp.

abilities.name: Age
abilities.prose: The following stats describe dragons of average size. Younger dragons may have up to 3 HD less and ¼ or ½ as much treasure. Older dragons may have up to 3 HD more and twice as much treasure.

abilities.name: Lairs
abilities.prose: A dragon’s treasure is always kept in its well-hidden lair and is seldom unguarded.

magicItems.name: Dagger +2, +3 vs orcs, goblins, and kobolds

potion_of_healing.name: Potion of Healing
manual: Has one of two effects on the character who drinks it:
Healing a living subject: Restores 1d6+1 hit points of damage. This cannot grant more hit points than the subject’s normal maximum.
Curing paralysis: Paralysing effects are negated.
Drinking a potion while already under the effects of another potion is dangerous:
Sickness: The character is completely disabled for 3 turns, due to sickness.
Cancellation: The effects of both potions are cancelled.
This rule does not apply to potions with instantaneous or permanent duration.

staff_of_snakes.name: Staff of Snakes
manual: A magical staff that has the power to transform into a snake, on command.
Divine magic: Usable by divine spell casters only.
In melee: Treated as a staff with a +1 magic bonus to attacks and damage.
On a successful hit: Upon a human-sized (or smaller) creature, the wielder of the staff may speak the command word, causing it to transform into a serpent and coil around the victim.
Victims: Must save versus spells or be immobilised in the coils of the snake. Victims are completely helpless while held by the snake (1d4 turns, or released as the wielder of the staff commands).
Snake: Has AC 5 [14], HD 3 (20hp), and a movement rate of 60’ (20’).
When the victim is released: The snake returns to the owner and transforms back into a staff. (At this point, it is healed of any damage it has suffered.)
If the snake is killed: It does not return to its staff form, becoming non-magical.
No charges: Does not use charges; may be used any number of times.
Usage: Spell casters. Some staves may only be used by either arcane or divine spell casters (this is noted in the item’s description).
Dimensions: 2” thick, 6’ long.
Charges: Unless noted, magic staves contain 3d10 charges when found.
Although magic-users are generally only allowed to use daggers in combat, they are able to use the staff of power, staff of striking, and staff of wizardry in melee.

cursed_scroll.name: Cursed Scroll
manual: One use only: When a scroll is read, the words disappear.
Light: A scroll can only be used if there is enough light to read by.

curses.name: Transformation
curses.prose: The reader changes into a harmless creature (e.g. a frog).

curses.name: Summoning
curses.prose: A wandering monster appears next to the reader and attacks (gaining surprise). The monster is of equal level to the reader.

curses.name: Lost item
curses.prose: A magic item in the reader’s possession vanishes. The referee may select the item or choose it at random.

curses.name: Energy drain
curses.prose: The reader permanently loses one experience level (or Hit Die). This incurs a loss of one Hit Die of hit points, as well as all other benefits due to the lost level (e.g. spells, saving throws, etc.). A character’s XP is reduced to halfway between the former and new levels. A person who loses all levels dies.

curses.name: Ability score re-roll
curses.prose: The player must re-roll the character’s prime requisite.

curses.name: Slow healing
curses.prose: The reader’s healing capacity is reduced. Natural healing takes double the normal amount of time, and healing spells only cure half the normal number of hit points.

manual_notes: Rough treatment of jewellery (e.g. crushing, intense heat or fire, lightning) can damage it, reducing its value by 50%.

When a treasure type indicates the presence of multiple gems or pieces of jewellery, the referee may combine the values, as desired. For example, a roll of five 50gp value gems may be placed as a single 250gp gem, a 100gp gem and three 50gp gems, or any other combination.
